title_en: Regulations on the Administration of Chinese Employees of Foreign Diplomatic and Consular Missions in China

articles.content_en:
Article 6 A foreign diplomatic mission or consular post in China shall enter into a service agreement with the foreign affairs service institution designated by the local competent foreign affairs service authority, specifying the protection of rights and interests of Chinese employees, applicable laws, dispute resolution, foreign affairs service fees, etc.; the foreign affairs service institution shall enter into a labor contract with the Chinese employee, specifying the auxiliary and service work content and labor remuneration of the Chinese employee in the foreign diplomatic mission or consular post.
The competent foreign affairs service authority and the foreign affairs service institution shall improve their management level and enhance service quality.

Article 7 After the foreign affairs service institution enters into a labor contract with a Chinese employee, the competent foreign affairs service authority shall issue a Chinese Employee Certificate to the Chinese employee as his or her work certificate.
The format of the Chinese Employee Certificate shall be uniformly prescribed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Article 8 A Chinese employee shall abide by the laws and regulations of China, perform the obligations specified in the labor contract, shall not commit any act that endangers national security or harms public interests, and shall not carry out activities in the capacity of a diplomatic agent or consular officer.

Article 9 Disputes relating to the service agreement as specified in the first paragraph of Article 6 of these Regulations shall be resolved in the manner agreed upon in the service agreement; disputes relating to the labor contract shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Mediation and Arbitration of Labor Disputes.

Article 10 No unit or individual, other than the institutions specified in these Regulations, shall provide employment services for Chinese employees to foreign diplomatic missions or consular posts in China. No Chinese citizen shall be privately employed by a foreign diplomatic mission or consular post in China without following the procedures specified in these Regulations.
Any violation of the provisions of these Regulations shall be handled by the competent foreign affairs service authority in coordination with relevant departments according to law.
Article 11 The Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall, in accordance with these Regulations, formulate specific measures for the administration of Chinese employees.
Article 12 These Regulations shall come into force as of January 1, 2026.
